StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter, but the sim deliberately does NOT add: on_stack appends a new (turns_left, damage) fuse to self.bombs and sets self.amount to the shortest fuse. That is the sim's hand-rolled workaround for the missing PowerInstanceType (see the InstanceType entry), and it is the RIGHT approximation -- C#'s Amount is a per-instance turn counter, so summing two instances' counters (what plain Power.on_stack would do) would be meaningless. Recorded as a deliberate divergence rather than faithful because the mechanism genuinely differs and the sim's own docstring (powers.py:3750-3753) says so.

InstanceType.issue: RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass): `deliberate-divergence` -> `gap`. LIVE 2026-07-30, bound to `power_cmd/G5` per this batch's brief rather than re-derived: `audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json` guard G5 ("No PowerInstanceType (Instanced / InstancedPerApplier) distinction in FindExistingInstanceForStacking") was settled LIVE in round 11 with its own executed witness (Automation/Panache, `.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/seam-power-cmd-g5-automation2.py`) and explicitly names The Bomb among its 11 ported Instanced/InstancedPerApplier sites. Per binding rule 3 this entry inherits that liveness rather than re-arguing the mechanism; what this record adds is that the_bomb's OWN reachability was independently demonstrated (see below) and matches G5's finding. PowerInstanceType.Instanced (TheBombPower.cs:23) means every application is an independently tracked instance with its own Amount and its own DynamicVars.Damage, where the sim's PowerCmd.apply merges by power id via on_stack (cmds.py:567-570, current line numbers). **REACHABILITY: two live fuses are plainly reachable.** The Bomb is a ported Uncommon Colorless Skill with NO Exhaust keyword (cards/colorless_skills.py:750-778, re-verified 2026-07-30, mirroring TheBomb.cs:23-26 whose CanonicalKeywords is empty), so it can simply be played on two consecutive turns. EXECUTED 2026-07-26: play it, end the turn, play it again -- the sim holds ONE `the_bomb` power whose fuse list is [[2, 40], [3, 40]] and whose `amount` is `min(turns for turns, _ in self.bombs)` == 2 (powers.py:3770-3772), where C# holds TWO TheBombPower instances with Amount 2 and Amount 3. **WHAT IS AND IS NOT REPRODUCED.** The DAMAGE is exact, and this unit is one of only two of G5's eleven ported units that acknowledges the distinction at all: each fuse carries its own turns_left and its own damage (powers.py:3768, :3771, set_damage at :3774-3777), the turn-end pass explodes every fuse at <= 1 independently and decrements the rest (:3785-3788), and the power only expires when the list empties (:3799-3800). The STATE is not reproduced, and that is why this is a gap rather than a divergence with the same observable outcome (binding rule 2). A different power list (one entry where the game has two) and a different amount (2 where the game shows 2 and 3) is not an internal detail: full_env.py:412 encodes EVERY ALL_POWERS id as a presence bit plus a signed amount at two scales, so the game's two-instance state cannot even be represented in the sim's observation, and any power-list comparison sees one entry for two. The second residue was already named on this entry before it was graded dd, and stands: an effect that removed 'a' Bomb would remove all of them in the sim, and set_damage always writes the NEWEST fuse (:3777), which is correct only because TheBomb.cs:30 calls SetDamage immediately after applying. **RULE 3:** the identical G5 mechanism is `gap` on power/rolling_boulder, whose two-instance case is reachable exactly the same way (a non-exhausting ported Colorless card played twice). Grading it `deliberate-divergence` here and `gap` there was a rule-3 break, and this is the site that moves: a good workaround makes the gap SMALLER -- the damage is right where rolling_boulder's is arithmetically 5 short on two consecutive turns -- not absent.

Hook.BeforeSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, called for the player side at CombatManager.cs:1179 -- BEFORE DoTurnEnd (:1191) and FlushPlayerHand (:1296) -- and the sim's on_player_turn_end is exactly that point (combat.py:654, before _process_turn_end_cards at :658 and the flush at :661-662). The Amount > 1 -> Decrement / else explode-then-Remove structure matches (TheBombPower.cs:44-57 vs powers.py:3785-3800). NOTE this is the plain pass, not an Early one, so power/plating's BeforeSideTurnEndEarly block correctly precedes it in the game -- the phase gap recorded on that unit is the sim's failure to guarantee it, and The Bomb damages ENEMIES, so the two do not actually contend.
